synthesis: Across this five-day period, three dominant narratives have emerged and shifted dramatically. First, Middle East geopolitical risk migrated from tail hedge to base case and back again, with energy markets repricing continuously: initial escalation (Iran attacks, Strait of Hormuz tensions) compressed equity risk premiums and extended Fed pause expectations, but emerging peace deal prospects then collapsed the geopolitical risk premium by May 6, flooding petrodollar-dependent economies with capital while reducing energy-transition urgency. Second, the labor market bifurcation deepened as headline ADP employment (109K in April) masked a structural crack: large firms continue hiring while small business decelerates, signaling consumption vulnerability that constrains margin expansion narratives essential to justify current equity multiples at compressed duration. Third, irreversible US-China tech bifurcation accelerated: China monetized advanced semiconductor cost advantages through DeepSeek's $50B funding and demonstrated 25 percent global advanced manufacturing share, while simultaneous US pre-deployment AI review regimes and data center restrictions locked non-incumbent vendors out of scaling paths, concentrating both energy and compute structures in state-aligned players and compressing Western allocator optionality.
themes: Middle East de-escalation pricing collapses geopolitical risk premium
Labor market bifurcation masks consumption vulnerability below headlines
China advances manufacturing dominance and AI monetization
US regulatory capture concentrates AI scaling to incumbents
Capital flows rotate toward alternatives and de-risked yield generation
